chunks: Abu Ja'far Ibn Babawayh said: Muhammad ibn Uthman al-Amari (may his spirit be sanctified) narrated that he said:
By Allah, the Master of this Affair attends the pilgrimage season every year; he sees the people and knows them, and they see him, but they do not recognize him.

key_terms.صَاحِبَ الْأَمْرِ: The Master of the Affair (referring to the Imam)
key_terms.قُدِّسَ سِرُّهُ: May his spirit be sanctified (a honorific for the narrator)
key_terms.وَلَا يَعْرِفُونَهُ: And they do not recognize him

ai.seo_question: Does the Imam of the Occultation attend Hajj every year?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Hasan ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar’s *Kitab al-Ghaybah* highlights the doctrine of the Imam's physical presence during the Major Occultation, specifically during Hajj. It underscores the concept of *al-Ru'ya bi-la Ta'rif* (seeing without recognizing), a key Shia theological point illustrating that the Imam is among the people but veiled from their full recognition by divine will.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 329 - Abu Ja’far Ibn Babawayh says: Muhammad Ibn Uthman Amari narrated that
by Allah, the Master of this Affair attends the Hajj every year; he sees the people and knows them and they also see him, but don’t recognize him.
